issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a parameterless milk method (messageOnMilk() returning a String and used in Main as m.messageOnMilk()), but the solution changes the Milkable interface to messageOnMilk(double volume) and updates Seal and Goat accordingly. This signature mismatch prevents students from implementing the interface as described and from using the method calls in the provided Main template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable interface and its implementations consistent with the problem statement and template by changing messageOnMilk(double volume) to a parameterless method messageOnMilk() returning String, and update Seal and Goat implementations to return the specified string format (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). Alternatively, if the volume parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template Main.java to document and use messageOnMilk(double) accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument Milkable.messageOnMilk() that returns a string like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked", but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) and implements it with a volume parameter and different return text (e.g. "Seal X is milked (1.0L)"). This mismatch in method signature and expected return value creates a direct mapping and compilation inconsistency (the template/Main calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments) and confuses students about the required interface contract and return format.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem and template by changing the Milkable interface to declare messageOnMilk() with no parameters returning String, and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning the exact form "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if volume is intended, update the problem statement and template/Main to use messageOnMilk(double volume) consistently and document the expected return format.
